findings.title: lane_sizes accepts overflow for unset lanes
findings.problem: Overflow is rejected only when a lane is set explicitly. Unset lanes are fitted to a minimum of 1 each, so a small pool (for example pool 2, reserve 2, available 1) yields heavy+light+jobs = 3 above the cap with no error. The spec says any configuration above pool - reserve is rejected. Also the reserve >= pool case silently gives capacity max(1, ...), which voids the ingest-reserve guarantee with no warning.
findings.impact: Dashboards can take the whole pool and ingest may find no connection; AC6 overflow rejection is only partly met. Reachable only on tiny pool/reserve combinations; reachability not confirmed against deployed config.
findings.recommendation: Raise CliAnalyticsStorageConfigError whenever sizes.total > available (and when reserve >= pool), regardless of whether lanes were set explicitly; add a test for pool 2 / reserve 2.
findings.check_notes: lane_sizes raises when reserve leaves none and whenever sizes.total > available, set or not

fix.change: lane_sizes raises when sizes.total > pool - reserve (set or not) and when reserve leaves no connection

findings.title: Branches route mis-parses project names
findings.problem: get_project_branches assigns the path value to filters.projects, which is parsed as a comma list, so a project name containing a comma becomes several projects. A real project named like the UNATTRIBUTED_PROJECT sentinel is treated as the unattributed project. The route also always takes the live heavy path because ranking_eligible refuses any projects filter or project_unattributed, which contradicts the docs claim that it uses the rollup when eligible.
findings.impact: Wrong or merged rows for such project names; docs overstate rollup use. Reachability of comma and sentinel names depends on real project data and was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Set the resolved filter's projects to [project_name] after resolve (bypass comma splitting), disambiguate the sentinel, and correct the docs about rollup eligibility.
findings.check_notes: route sets f.projects=[project_name] after resolve, sentinel documented, docs say it always runs live

fix.change: branches route sets the resolved filter's projects to [project_name] (no comma split, scope intersected); docs state it always runs live and the sentinel is reserved

findings.title: Session auth read bypasses dashboard lanes
findings.problem: get_session_detail calls reader.authorize_session outside dashboard_request and job_scope. The engine classifies an unnamed acquire with no request stats and no job scope as a job, so the auth read takes one of the 2 jobs slots and the 30 s plain acquire timeout (503) instead of the light lane and the dashboard 504. It is outside _statement_timeout_as_504 too.
findings.impact: Session detail auth queues behind refresh jobs and can 503, defeating the light lane and the jobs allowance isolation. Confirmed by reading the router call site.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the authorize_session call in dashboard_request('light') (and the 504 mapping), or move it inside the handler's light request; add the method to LANE_BY_METHOD style coverage.
findings.check_notes: authorize_session now wrapped in dashboard_request('light') in the handler

fix.change: new handler.authorize_session runs in the light lane; session detail route uses it under the 504 mapping

findings.title: Lane slot wait bounded by acquire timeout
findings.problem: dashboard_slot wraps the lane-slot wait in wait_for(ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_S) and raises DashboardAcquireTimeout, while the spec bounds the slot wait only by the 540 s budget. engine.acquire then starts a second full timeout for cap and pool, so one request can wait about twice the setting, contradicting docs that say the timeout bounds slot and connection together. A pooled-connection wait past the timeout stays a plain 503.
findings.impact: Queued requests fail at 30 s rather than waiting for their budget, and the documented timeout semantics are wrong. Not re-read in source by this triage; lens-derived.
findings.recommendation: Align code and spec: leave the slot wait bounded by the request budget only, pass the remaining timeout into engine.acquire, and map the pool wait timeout to the same 504 subtype; fix the docs wording.
findings.check_notes: dashboard_slot waits on the gate bounded by the request budget only; docs reworded

fix.change: dashboard_slot no longer wraps the slot wait in the acquire timeout (budget only); docs corrected

findings.title: Live session merge runs in light lane
findings.problem: _rollup_ranking_read runs the read inside dashboard_request('light'). serve_cohort then calls _merge_live_sessions, which runs live gather_ranking/gather_cohort statements (up to 2000 sessions) in the light lane. Only a rollup refusal re-enters the heavy gate; the spec says a merge that runs live re-enters it too. Warm-up also holds a light slot and a jobs slot together.
findings.impact: Heavy live statements consume light-lane capacity and can starve light requests. Reachability of large merges not confirmed; lens-derived.
findings.recommendation: Re-enter the heavy gate for the live merge (or have the reader signal that it ran live), and add a test like the refusal one.
findings.check_notes: _rollup_ranking_read re-enters HEAVY when live_merge is signalled

fix.change: light-lane ranking read raises LiveMergeNeeded instead of merging live; handler re-reads in the heavy lane

findings.title: Overview top-10 not served by ranking rollup

findings.impact: A required spec item is only partly implemented; Overview top-10 still runs the live heavy statements. Whether this was descoped intentionally was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Serve Overview top-10 from the ranking rollup when ranking_eligible, or record the descoping against the spec.
findings.check_notes: descoping recorded in the storage guide; no code serves Overview top-10 from ranking rows

fix.change: descoping recorded in cli-analytics-storage.md: Overview top-10 keeps its Overview rollup, only /repositories and /projects read the ranking rows
